headline: Binder design moves toward multi-variant, all-atom, and latent-space affinity-guided generation
label: Computational Antibody And Binder Design
summary: Five new reports span all-atom de novo design, multi-variant antibody optimization, and peptide binder generation, with training-data simulation for peptide binding.
synthesis: The dominant thread is binder design conditioned on richer objectives than affinity to one fixed target. Germinal Multi optimizes a single paratope across multiple antigen variants, reporting binding to EGFR variants and SARS-CoV-2 neutralization. An antigen-specific protein language model guides CDR optimization for antibody design. For PDZ-binding peptides, design proceeds along directions in a shared PDZ-PBM latent space learned from affinity prediction. Pallatom2 jointly models sequence, backbone, side chains and target contacts at the atom level (65.9M parameters), with reported experimental validation. VReceptor addresses data scarcity by simulating sequence-dependent peptide binding with pharmacophore-inspired weighting. Modalities and validation standards differ across items, so results are not directly comparable.
